question: Assume today is 2026-08-17. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States in August 2026 (the number of housing units at an annual rate, as in '1,300,000'), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release.

target.what: Seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026, as first reported in the Census Bureau/HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release (units started during the month, expressed at an annual rate)
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Monthly New Residential Construction (New Residential Construction, series under Construction Reports C20)
target.cadence: monthly, released mid-month for the prior month (August 2026 data would first be published around mid-September 2026, after the cutoff)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-08-17 cutoff, so no August 2026 observation exists; must be forecast from pre-cutoff data. 'Privately-owned' excludes publicly owned starts (small share). 'Housing starts' counts units on which construction has begun, not permits or completions. SAAR is t

candidates.hypothesis: Recent monthly private housing starts SAAR (through June/July 2026) plus seasonal and trend patterns anchor a short-horizon forecast; August typically shows a modest seasonal-adjustment-neutral continuation of the recent level with month-to-month noise.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly private housing starts SAAR (and single-family vs 2+ units) for 2024, 2025, and Jan-Jul 2026 as published before 2026-08-17; also the prior-year August value and recent 3-6 month trend.
search_hints: Census Bureau new residential construction housing starts June 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Permits precede starts; the permit-to-start ratio (starts SAAR / permits SAAR) is fairly stable near 1, so August permits level times that ratio constrains August starts. Permits for August 2026 are also unreleased, so use July 2026 permits and recent permit trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly private housing units authorized by building permits SAAR for 2025 and Jan-Jul 2026; historical starts-to-permits ratio by month.
search_hints: housing units authorized by building permits 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Units under construction and completions reflect the pipeline; a high under-construction stock with slowing completions implies starts continue at a moderate pace. Provides a consistency check on the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Housing units under construction and completions SAAR for 2025 and 2026 months before cutoff.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts for August 2026 housing starts (e.g., from banks, Fannie Mae, NAHB, or consensus panels) made before the cutoff give a direct point estimate to compare against model routes.
candidates.data_to_find: Any pre-2026-08-17 forecast of August 2026 or Q3 2026 housing starts SAAR; NAHB/Wells Fargo housing market index and single-family starts expectations.

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage rates, homebuilder sentiment, and any policy/credit shocks before the cutoff shift the level of starts; a rate decline raises starts with a lag. Quantify direction and rough magnitude.
candidates.data_to_find: 30-year mortgage rate path through mid-2026, NAHB HMI through July/August 2026, and any housing policy changes; builder sentiment trend.

candidates.hypothesis: August SAAR relates to the unadjusted August count via the Census seasonal factor; historical August seasonal factors and typical month-to-month SAAR volatility bound the forecast error.
candidates.data_to_find: Census seasonal factors for housing starts by month (recent vintage) and historical August month-over-month SAAR changes.
search_hints: Census housing starts seasonal factors table

candidates.hypothesis: Starts are the sum of four Census regions; regional permit trends (South, West, Midwest, Northeast) can be aggregated to a national level and reveal whether national momentum is broad or concentrated.
candidates.data_to_find: Regional private housing starts and permits SAAR for 2025 and 2026 months before cutoff.
search_hints: building permits south west midwest northeast 2026

methods.rationale: Seasonal-naive year-over-year route: August 2025 starts (1,291k) scaled by a modest decline factor reflecting weak sentiment, rising rates, and falling construction pipeline. Shared dependency: relies on the Equibles series (p12) being consistent with Census definitions.

methods.label: m3

methods.rationale: Component decomposition: SF starts (895k) with slight softening plus MF starts (532k) reverting from the June spike toward the 3-month average. Sums the two non-overlapping segments. Shared dependency: both components from the same June Census release; MF volatility is the dominant uncertainty.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p57: Permits are a different quantity than housing starts; the role uses permits as a pipeline level for starts, and the conversion ratio a1 is a starts-to-permits ratio, but the evidence is total per

kept.name: August 2026 starts-to-June-permits ratio
kept.rationale: Historically starts/permits ratio hovers near 1.0; June 2026 starts (1,430k) exceeded permits (1,370k) due to a multifamily surge (p55), so August starts likely revert toward or slightly below the permit level. Wide range reflects month-to-month noise and the June gap.
kept.applies_when: Permit pipeline is the binding constraint on starts and the June multifamily spike mean-reverts.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that August multifamily starts sustain the June surge, pushing starts well above permits.

kept.name: August 2026 change factor vs August 2025 starts
kept.rationale: Weak builder sentiment (HMI 34, p76), rising mortgage rates (6.66% end-July, p61), and declining under-construction stock (p46) point to a modest year-over-year decline from August 2025's 1,291k (p12). Range reflects uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: Year-over-year momentum in starts is broadly stable with a slight downward tilt from weak demand.
kept.falsified_by: A sharp rate decline or policy stimulus before August that lifts starts well above last year.

kept.name: August 2026 SF starts change factor vs June 2026
kept.rationale: SF starts have fallen three consecutive months (p140) on high prices and rates; modest further softening expected by August.
kept.falsified_by: A rebound in SF permits or sales that reverses the SF downtrend.

kept.name: August 2026 MF starts change factor vs June 2026
kept.rationale: June MF starts spiked 76% (p55/p137) after a 41% May plunge; such volatility typically mean-reverts. MF permits declining (p59) and under-construction falling (p48) support a pullback.
kept.applies_when: The June multifamily surge is a one-off and reverts toward the 3-month average (p56 ~445k).
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of sustained multifamily permit strength or large project starts in July-August.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
